title: Data Augmentation in the Pipeline 🎨
description: Integrate Keras preprocessing layers and tf.image ops into your input pipeline.

slides.title: Augmentation Inside the Model or the Pipeline? 🎯
slides.content:
# Two Integration Points

1. **As part of the model**: use `tf.keras.layers` like `RandomFlip`, `RandomRotation` as the first layers of your network.
2. **In the tf.data pipeline**: apply `tf.image` operations inside a `.map()` call.

Pros of pipeline augmentation:
- Runs on CPU in parallel with GPU training.
- No overhead during inference (not part of saved model).

Pros of model‑integrated:
- Simpler, model‑self‑contained, can export with augmentation for deployment if needed.

slides.title: Augmentation in tf.data using map
slides.codeSnippet:
def augment(image, label):
    image = tf.image.random_flip_left_right(image)
    image = tf.image.random_brightness(image, max_delta=0.1)
    image = tf.image.random_contrast(image, lower=0.8, upper=1.2)
    return image, label

dataset = dataset.map(augment, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

quizData.question: Augmentation inside the tf.data pipeline is applied only during training, not evaluation, if you prepare separate datasets.
quizData.explanation: You typically create a training dataset with augmentation and a validation dataset without.

slides.title: Using Keras Preprocessing Layers in the Pipeline
slides.content:
# For Consistency, You Can Map Layers

You can instantiate a layer and call it inside a map function:
```python
flip = tf.keras.layers.RandomFlip('horizontal')
rotate = tf.keras.layers.RandomRotation(0.1)

def augment_keras(image, label):
    image = flip(image, training=True)
    image = rotate(image, training=True)
    return image, label
```
The `training=True` ensures randomness only during training.

slides.title: Consistency Matters ⚖️
slides.content: If you use augmentation in the pipeline, remember to **not** apply it to validation/test datasets. Build separate pipelines for training and evaluation.
